To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the statistics of spike trains is strongly affected by the temporal structure of the input to the cell, which can be described by a correlation structure, the power spectrum of the input.

(i) the spike train statistics of a tonically spiking neuron is strongly affected by the input correlation structure, and (ii) we have derived a theory to compute the interspike interval distribution in the case of arbitrary input correlations, and (iii) we have verified this theory by simulations for three paradigmatical situations that lead to non white noise input.
the statistics of the spike train of a neuron driven by correlated input is not simply given by the statistics of the interspike intervals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the statistical structure of spike trains of a neuron under non Poisson stimulation.
the analysis of the statistical structure of neural spike trains under non-Poissonian stimulation.
the statistical structure of neural spiketrains under non Poisson stimulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the statistics of spike trains in the brain can be explained only if the input statistics are taken into account.

, in the case of a colored noise input, the spike train statistics is not simply Poissonian, but it has a non-trivial structure that can be derived from a simple formula, which is a consequence of our theoretical approach.
the statistics of the interspike intervals is a function of the statistics of the input spike train.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the statistics of the spike trains is not only determined by the statistics of the presynaptic spike train but also by the statistics of presynaptic refractory periods and synaptic plasticity.
the statistics of neural spiking depends on the statistics of the stimulation.
the temporal structure of input spike trains can have severe effects on the spike train statistics of the postsynaptic neurons, even if the input rate is constant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in general, the interspike interval distributions of a tonically spiking neuron under colored noise stimulation can be very different from the Poisson distribution.
the interspike interval distribution of a neuron driven by colored noise can be very different from the one of a Poisson process, even if the mean firing rate is the same.
the statistics of neural spiking is strongly affected by the correlation structure of presynaptic spike activity and that this can be understood with a simple theory.
